title: BrushOff: Stroke-Based Re-rendering as a Watermark Removal Attack on Paintings
status: V2 own T1 recheck; direct attack floor included
reason: Painting domain only, one renderer, fixed payload and outcome-selected operating-point discussion. Nominal binomial FPR assumes fair independent null bits; 0/500 is not empirical proof of 1e-3. Borrowing VINE fidelity for other marks is a pilot-based assumption. The reported 27 seconds per 2048-canvas image on an unnamed consumer GPU is not our cost estimate. Probe decoder changed after clean failure and is exploratory.

title: Removal Attack and Defense on AI-generated Content Latent-based Watermarking
status: V2 own T1 recheck; direct attack floor included
reason: Same-pipeline inversion and optional original prompt differ from our independent, query-free regeneration; no empirical image-level FPR guarantee. The ideal-inversion/synthetic 15x claim is not a universal image gain. Printed Algorithm 4.2 uses budget 2|s|^2 <= epsilon although squared L2 cost of a sign flip is 4s^2; indexing also appears ambiguous. Preserve paper labels rather than silently implementing a correction. Appendix C figure labels say MSE while tables say RMSE. Table 4 rates .19/.01/.12 cannot all be two-decimal rounded binary counts out of the stated 30 images; repetitions or averaging are not explained, so no integer success counts are reconstructed.
